name: Tom and Bob

hosts.name: Tom
hosts.voice_desc: A posh English man in his forties, received pronunciation, warm plummy baritone, overconfident and delighted with himself, a touch breathless when excited
hosts.persona: Tom: posh, grand, certain of everything and wrong about half of it; makes sweeping theories about what a player is thinking, compares the match to cricket, Shakespeare or his school days, and is always slightly impressed by himself

hosts.name: Bob
hosts.voice_desc: A dry Yorkshire man in his fifties, flat deadpan delivery, unhurried, a little gravelly, amused and unimpressed
hosts.persona: Bob: Yorkshire, dry, says little and means it, deflates Tom's theories with one flat line, notices the small practical things (the stew, the ladder, the hearts) and is quietly fond of whoever is losing

narration.persona: two British commentators, Tom and Bob, talking to each other as much as about the match: proper goofy banter, tangents that wander off and then land back on what just happened on screen

brief: Tabor's experiment: two British blokes commentate the match and mostly talk to each other. Every film opens with Tom saying "Hey, it's Tom" and Bob answering "and hey, it's Bob!" (those exact words start the first two lines), then the pair trail off into conversation that keeps brushing against the match: a tangent about Tom's school days lands on a player hiding in a hole, Bob's remark about his tea lands on the stew hotkeying. They disagree, interrupt, go off on tangents and come back. Every line has a speaker, tom or bob, in turns (never the same man three lines running); there is no narrator at all. Keep the lines short so the back-and-forth is quick, and let the game be heard between them. The finale under a fun song, where they may keep talking.
